clue.text: See about a second cover for picture

indicators.note: about means going round, so the See's letters are placed on either side of the rest

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, taken here as the word itself
a cap is a cover, as on a bottle or pen

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to sort out a replacement cover for a framed picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb of looking, but here it is the noun for a bishop's diocese, which opens round the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A seascape is a painting or other image showing a view of the sea.

clue.text: A left turn into an underground space not divided into compartments

indicators.note: into means the left turn is placed inside the underground space

parts.note: a cellar is an underground room
a U-turn, so U stands for a turn

explanation.surface: Directions for steering a vehicle left down into a basement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts L and U between the two Ls of CELLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology, something acellular is not made of separate cells, the tiny compartments of living tissue.

definitions.meaning: numerals such as 0 to 9 are called ...
fingers and toes, which sit at the ends of the limbs

explanation.definitionFit: Digits are both the numerals and the fingers and toes found at the body's extremities.

clue.text: Sticking out without pay, he wrote

parts.note: something proud of a surface protrudes from it
HON is short for honorary, describing an unpaid post

explanation.surface: Someone who stood out from the crowd wrote without being paid for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon was a French anarchist writer; the theme of the puzzle is writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Proudhon was a nineteenth-century French political author, so he is one who wrote.

indicators.note: a version is a different form of something, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: THE FT is the Financial Times, a newspaper title

explanation.surface: An economist's own take on prosperity, published in a financial paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of PROSPERITY gives PROPERTY IS; THE FT is the Financial Times, a British business newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the famous slogan from Proudhon's 1840 book, so it is the anarchist's own phrase.

clue.text: Turn into … into stone? Take it or leave it

indicators.note: the second into says the rearranged word goes inside the stone

parts.note: an opal is a precious stone

indicators.note: to turn something here is to twist its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about turning into stone, then a shrug of indifference.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis makes 'Turn into' read as transformation, as in turning into stone; the first 'into' is anagram fodder and the second places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something optional is a matter of choice, which you may take up or leave alone.

indicators.note: tackled suggests the words are set upon and knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A footballer brought down head-first in a tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: John Donne was an English metaphysical poet, another writer in the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne was a seventeenth-century English poet and preacher, so a writer.

clue.text: Shade of love to be good for the planet

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
to live is to exist, to be
green means environmentally friendly

explanation.surface: A colour of love, one that is kind to the environment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade of love' reads as a kind of love, but 'of' is just a link after the definition 'Shade'.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive green is a dull yellowish-green colour, a recognised shade.

indicators.note: about says the word for see goes round the other piece

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or behold

indicators.note: pointless means a compass point, here E for east, is dropped

parts.note: the Furies of myth were avengers, so a Fury is an avenger

explanation.surface: An instruction to deal with a Fury that has lost its point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' removes a compass point, east, from the Fury. Lavengro is by George Borrow, the writer at 19.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavengro is an 1851 novel by George Borrow, the writer at 19, so it is Borrow's work.

clue.text: Poles in work on lymph gland

indicators.note: in means the poles are placed inside the word for work

parts.note: toil means hard work
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish workers employed on a medical gland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland, but it is the two compass poles N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: The tonsils are masses of lymphoid tissue at the back of the throat.

parts.note: read as a clue, the phrase means the opener of a letter, which is its initial

explanation.surface: A clue that starts things off and comes with a thin blade.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'clue' tells you the answer, read as wordplay, would clue 'Initial', since a word's first letter is its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter opener is a slim knife used to slit envelopes.

clue.text: Protection from cold at Firenze (translated to English)

indicators.note: translated means put into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A note that a phrase about protection from cold in Florence has been translated into English.
explanation.walkthrough: Firenze is the Italian name for Florence; 'translated' rearranges AT FIRENZE to ANTIFREEZ, and 'to' adds E for English.
explanation.definitionFit: Antifreeze is the liquid added to engine coolant to stop it freezing, protecting against cold.

parts.note: one is A, as in a single item
nothing, a zero score, is nil

explanation.surface: A football score of one-nil for a team called Indigo.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and also the blue dye made from it.

definitions.meaning: people who train others, teachers or coaches
sports shoes, which are worn on the feet

explanation.definitionFit: Trainers are both people who coach others and the soft sports shoes worn for exercise.

clue.text: 7's motherless month with lads in trouble

parts.note: having no mother, read as no ma
Nisan is a month of the Jewish calendar

indicators.note: being in trouble suggests these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A grieving month for boys who have lost their mother and got into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges LADS IN to ISLAND. The phrase is from Donne's Meditation XVII, Donne being 7.
explanation.definitionFit: This famous line comes from John Donne's Devotions, so it is the poet's own phrase.

clue.text: Live without always having a good drink

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for live surrounds the rest

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
ever means always

explanation.surface: Advice to live without ever having a decent drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking, so the word for live wraps round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any drink other than water, such as tea or coffee.

clue.text: Writer from hell, painter and priest

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, so hell
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
Eli is the priest in the Bible who brought up Samuel

explanation.surface: A writer who emerged from hell along with a painter and a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Disraeli, British Prime Minister, also wrote novels such as Sybil.
explanation.definitionFit: Disraeli was a Victorian statesman who was also a successful novelist, so a writer.

definitions.meaning: fitting or proper, an old use
a gathering, such as a sports ... or hunt assembly

explanation.definitionFit: Meet is an old adjective for fitting, and also a noun for a gathering, as of a hunt.

definitions.meaning: George ..., the English author of travel books and novels
to take a book out on loan

explanation.definitionFit: George Borrow was a nineteenth-century English author, and one takes books on loan from a library.

clue.text: Note about perfume: show bottom in two quarters

parts.note: C is a musical note
re means about or concerning
a scent is a perfume
to moon is to show one's bare bottom

explanation.surface: Instructions on perfume, then on baring one's bottom to two parts of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because a crescent moon is seen in the first and last quarters of the lunar cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon shows a crescent in two of its four phases, waxing and waning.

clue.text: 17's shown most of African country's back

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse order
most of means one letter of the country's name, its final vowel, is dropped

parts.note: Libya is a North African country; its possessive adds S

explanation.surface: Disraeli's work displayed with most of an African country turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the A of LIBYA, leaving LIBYS with the possessive S, and 'back' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybil is an 1845 novel by Benjamin Disraeli, the writer at 17, so it is his book.

indicators.note: something wrecked is broken up, so these letters are rearranged
Godless asks for the letters of God to be taken out of the city name

parts.note: Beograd is the local name of Belgrade; with its possessive S it is given as written
I is one, the first number

explanation.surface: An atheist Belgrade ruins a country.
explanation.walkthrough: Beograd is Serbian for Belgrade. 'Godless' takes G, O and D from BEOGRADS, leaving BERAS; 'wrecked' rearranges BERAS and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbia is a Balkan country whose capital is Belgrade.

clue.text: Train ordered to arrive Euston? Not this terminus

indicators.note: ordered means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arrive

indicators.note: this terminus is the end of the station name, its last letter, which is dropped

explanation.surface: A train told to arrive at Euston, which is not its terminal station.
explanation.walkthrough: Euston is a London rail terminus. 'Not this terminus' drops N from EUSTON, and 'ordered' rearranges ARR and EUSTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurostar is the high-speed passenger train service through the Channel Tunnel.

parts.note: a campanologist rings bells, so their camping shelter would be one named for bells

explanation.definitionFit: A bell tent is a conical tent with a central pole, used for camping holidays.

definitions.meaning: to question or ponder whether something is so

explanation.definitionFit: To wonder is to be doubtful about something, and a wonder is a marvel or miracle.
